🚨 NOW THAT’S A HECK OF A COINCIDENCE…

Today, a major FAA communications outage caused widespread disruption across some of the busiest airspace in the country.

According to officials, the incident involved a failure of the primary communications circuit — followed by the discovery that the backup fiber connection had already been physically severed during railroad construction in New Jersey.

The result: controllers temporarily lost critical radar data and radio communications, triggering ground stops and disruptions affecting major Northeast airports.

But here’s where the timing gets interesting…

⚠️ ON THE SAME DAY, a new government watchdog report warned about cybersecurity vulnerabilities within the nation’s aviation infrastructure — including threats involving hacking, spoofing and jamming.

The report also raised concerns about the FAA’s ability to comprehensively detect certain threats in real time.

So, to be clear:

❌ There is currently NO evidence that today’s FAA outage was caused by a cyberattack.

☑ Officials currently attribute it to a primary circuit failure combined with the previously damaged backup fiber.

But after everything we’ve been documenting lately involving cyberattacks, critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, “zero-day” reporting and warnings about attacks on U.S. systems, having a massive FAA communications failure occur the very same day a government report warns about aviation cyber vulnerabilities is one hell of a coincidence.

Two separate stories.

Same day.

Same critical infrastructure.

And definitely worth adding to the timeline. 👀
